extracted.intended_audience: playwrights, poets, dramatists, students and scholars of Indian aesthetics seeking to evoke or evaluate rasa
extracted.subtask_description: Applying Bharata Muni's Natyashastra Rasa theory to create or evaluate works of drama and literature so they successfully evoke a dominant emotional flavor (rasa) in a cultivated spectator (sahṛdaya). Emphasis is on integrating determinants, consequents, and transient states to produce authentic rasa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundamental criterion: successful evocation of rasa
rubrics_metrics.description: The fundamental criterion: does the work successfully evoke a rasa in the cultivated reader (sahṛdaya)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rasa is the aesthetic flavor or emotional essence experienced by a 'one with heart' (sahṛdaya). The work's primary test is whether it produces that rasa in such an audience, not merely whether it describes emotions.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Nine Rasas (Navarasa)
rubrics_metrics.description: The classical set of nine essential emotional flavors that a work may evoke: Śṛṅgāra (love/romance), Hāsya (laughter/mirth), Karuṇa (compassion/sorrow), Raudra (fury/wrath), Vīra (heroism/valor), Bhayānaka (fear/terror), Bībhatsa (disgust/aversion), Adbhuta (wonder/amazement), Śānta (peace/tranquility).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each rasa is a distinct evaluative target — a successful work will evoke one clear, dominant rasa (though combinations occur historically). The list includes presiding deities historically associated with each rasa; Śānta was added later (Abhinavagupta).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sthayibhava (stable emotions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eight permanent mental states that underlie each rasa: rati (love), hāsa (mirth), śoka (sorrow), krodha (anger), utsāha (energy), bhaya (terror), jugupsā (disgust), vismaya (astonishment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sthayibhava is the enduring emotion on which a rasa rests; a work must cultivate and sustain the appropriate sthayibhava in the audience to yield the corresponding rasa.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vibhava (determinants)
rubrics_metrics.description: The causes producing the emotion: Ālambana — the human object/substratum (the beloved, the enemy); Uddīpana — the excitants (moonlight, garden, weapon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dramatic/material determinants must be presented so they naturally give rise to the target sthayibhava; they are the narrative/imagistic causes that trigger the emotional state rather than merely naming it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anubhava (consequents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Observable effects of the emotion: gestures, expressions, voice changes. Includes the eight sāttvika bhāvas — involuntary physical signs (sweating, trembling, tears, voice break, hair standing on end, fainting, change of color, paralysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anubhavas are the visible/audible manifestations that confirm the emotion; skillful integration of anubhava makes the emotion believable. Sāttvika bhāvas are especially important to show inner intensity through involuntary reaction rather than explicit statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vyabhicāribhāva (transient ancillary states)
rubrics_metrics.description: The 33 fleeting ancillary feelings (e.g., shame, weariness, anxiety, pride, jealousy) that color and support the dominant emotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transient states should be used to texture and support the sthayibhava and rasa — they are not substitutes for the dominant stable emotion but provide realistic nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formula for rasa (composition rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rasa arises from the combination of vibhāva + anubhāva + vyabhicāribhāva acting upon the sthayibhava in a cultivated audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the compositional/analytic rule: successful aesthetic design must orchestrate determinants (causes), consequents (effects), and transient states so they operate on the stable emotion to produce rasa; failure in any element can prevent rasa from arising.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required audience: the Sahṛdaya
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'one with heart' — a spectator with aesthetic cultivation, emotional attunement, and artistic literacy. Without the sahṛdaya, no rasa arises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation must account for the intended cultivated audience; some work may not produce rasa in an untrained viewer. Aesthetic experience is co-produced — the creator must aim for the sensibility of the sahṛdaya.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the work evoke a clear, dominant rasa?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluative question: Does the work evoke a clear, dominant rasa?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity and dominance of a single rasa is a key measure. Ambiguous or muddled emotional targets weaken rasa; while complex works may suggest blends, a discernible primary rasa is central in classical evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of determinants and consequents
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluative question: Are determinants and consequents skillfully integrated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically assess whether the vibhāva (causes) and anubhāva (effects) are woven into the work so they naturally produce the sthayibhava, rather than feeling forced, decorative, or merely descriptive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional authenticity through technique, not assertion
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluative question: Does emotional authenticity emerge from technique, not stated assertion?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emotion should arise from enacted causes/effects and craft (imagery, gesture, voice), not from telling the audience what to feel or using explicit exposition. Anti-pattern: stating 'he was sad' without physicalized consequents and determinants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transport beyond entertainment toward expression of ultimate reality
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluative question: Does the work transport the spectator beyond entertainment toward the expression of ultimate reality?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond mere elicitation of feeling, classical Rasa aesthetics values works that move the spectator toward a contemplative or transfiguring insight — the rasa can point toward universals or soteriological/ontological dimensions.
